h1: The 6 Best Small Ultrasonic Cleaners of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Small Ultrasonic Cleaners: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 small ultrasonic cleaners for jewelry, retainers and eyewear, scored on tank size, frequency, noise, timers and UV extras.
summary: The Magnasonic 20oz is the best small ultrasonic cleaner because its 600 ml stainless tank, five cleaning modes and basket handle rings, glasses and small tools in one machine. The UMPOPO is the pick for retainers and mouthguards, with a UV-C step and sub-38dB running. Clelifove adds a two-year warranty to a UV retainer pod. For the toughest deposits, the VEVOR 1.3L runs at the lower 40 kHz.
intro: A small ultrasonic cleaner sounds like a single product category, but the tank size splits it into two jobs. Under about 250 ml you are cleaning a retainer or a ring, and the unit is basically a pod. Above 500 ml you can drop in eyeglasses, a watch band or a handful of tools. Buying the wrong size is the mistake that sends most of these back.

We reviewed six compact units from their specs, comparing tank volume, ultrasonic frequency, noise, timer options and extras like UV. Frequencies here run from 40 kHz to 48 kHz. Higher numbers are gentler on delicate surfaces, while 40 kHz cleans harder. Rankings weigh tank usefulness first, then noise and how clearly each listing describes its cycles.

products.name: Magnasonic 20oz Stainless Steel Ultrasonic Cleaner
products.verdict: A 600 ml stainless tank, five modes and a basket make it the most versatile small unit.
products.description:
The Magnasonic holds 20 oz (600 ml) in a stainless steel tank, runs at 42,000 Hz and offers five cleaning modes with a digital timer and display. A basket is included.

Its 600 ml volume is about double the 350 ml jewelry units, enough for glasses with the temples folded or a small tool set. The five modes are the reason it outranks the OSLTWI: you can choose a short cycle for rings and a longer one for tarnish.

Buy it if you clean more than jewelry. The caveat is that 42,000 Hz is near the harder end, so skip fragile or porous stones, and note the listing gives no noise figure.
products.idealFor: Households cleaning glasses, jewelry and small tools in one unit.
products.skipIf: You only clean a retainer and want the smallest pod.

products.name: UMPOPO 48kHz Ultrasonic Retainer Cleaner with UV-C
products.verdict: Quiet 48 kHz cleaning with a pulse-flow mode and a UV-C step for retainers.
products.description:
The UMPOPO runs at 48 kHz, has a UV-C lamp, claims noise under 38dB and offers a pulse-flow mode. Its cycle is 10 minutes of cleaning followed by 10 minutes of UV-C.

That sub-38dB figure is the quietest in this list, which suits a bedroom counter. It sits below the Magnasonic only because it is a retainer-focused pod, not a general-purpose tank, and the listing gives no tank volume.

It is the better buy for aligners, mouthguards and dental retainers. The caveat is that UV is an add-on step, not a replacement for brushing, and the missing capacity figure means you should check that your appliance fits.
products.idealFor: Retainer and mouthguard wearers who want a quiet nightstand cleaner.
products.skipIf: You want to clean glasses or tools.

products.name: Clelifove 48kHz Ultrasonic Retainer Cleaner with UV, 200 ml
products.verdict: A 200 ml UV pod with three cycle choices and a two-year warranty.
products.description:
The Clelifove has a 200 ml pod, runs at 48 kHz and has four UV lights under the lid. Its three modes are 5 minutes, 10 minutes and UV only, and the warranty is two years.

The two-year coverage is the longest in the group and a reason to pick it over the UMPOPO if reliability worries you. The UV-only mode lets you refresh a retainer without running the transducer. It ranks third because it states no noise figure, while the UMPOPO claims under 38dB.

Choose it for dental appliances and small jewelry. The caveat is size: 200 ml fits a retainer, not eyeglasses.
products.idealFor: Retainer users who value a longer warranty.
products.skipIf: You need to clean glasses or larger items.

products.name: OSLTWI 48kHz Ultrasonic Jewelry Cleaner, 350 ml
products.verdict: A light 350 ml jewelry cleaner with two modes and a one-touch selector.
products.description:
The OSLTWI holds 350 ml in a 304 stainless tank, runs at 48 kHz, weighs 0.57 kg and offers two cleaning modes with a one-touch selector.

The 350 ml size is right for rings, chains and watch bands, and 0.57 kg makes it easy to store. It trails the Magnasonic for flexibility, with two modes against five and a smaller tank. It ranks above KUNPHY because the listing describes its modes and weight.

Buy it if jewelry is the main job. The caveat is the missing basket and noise details, so check what ships in the box.
products.idealFor: Jewelry wearers cleaning rings and chains.
products.skipIf: You want a basket or five cycle options.

products.name: KUNPHY 46kHz Ultrasonic Jewelry Cleaner, 350 ml
products.verdict: A quiet 350 ml cleaner under 45dB with a short 3 minute timer.
products.description:
The KUNPHY runs at 46,000 Hz, holds 350 ml, claims noise below 45dB and has a 3 minute timer. The maker backs it with a one-year quality commitment.

It is quieter than the Magnasonic, which lists no noise figure, but louder than the UMPOPO's under 38dB. The fixed 3 minute timer is fine for light jewelry, yet it ranks below the OSLTWI because there is no second mode for heavier tarnish.

It suits daily rings and earrings. The caveat is the one-year commitment, half of the Clelifove warranty, and the single cycle length.
products.idealFor: Everyday jewelry cleaning with minimal fuss.
products.skipIf: You need a longer cycle for heavy tarnish.

products.name: VEVOR 1.3L 40kHz Ultrasonic Cleaner, 60W
products.verdict: The biggest tank here at 1.3 L, with a 60W 40 kHz transducer and 30 minute timer.
products.description:
The VEVOR holds 1.3 L in a 6.1 x 5.5 x 2.6 in 304 stainless tank, with a 60W transducer at 40 kHz, a 0 to 30 minute digital timer and 110V power.

The lower frequency cleans harder than the 46 to 48 kHz units, and the 1.3 L volume is double the Magnasonic's 600 ml. It ranks last because 40 kHz is rough on fragile items, and the shallow 2.6 in depth limits what fits.

Choose it for tools, razor heads and sturdy hardware. The caveat is the missing heater and the depth limit.
products.idealFor: Sturdy tools and hardware that need aggressive cleaning.
products.skipIf: You clean soft stones or plated jewelry.

methodology.description: Higher kHz is gentler and lower kHz cleans harder, so we match frequency to the intended use.

methodology.title: Noise
methodology.description: Published decibel figures matter for bedrooms and shared counters.

whatMatters.detail: Tank volume decides what physically fits. A 200 ml pod holds a retainer, 350 ml takes rings and watch bands, and 600 ml reaches eyeglasses. Check the stated millilitres, then compare them to the widest object you clean, remembering that items need to stay below the water line.

Frequency controls bubble size. Higher kHz makes smaller, gentler bubbles that suit delicate surfaces, while 40 kHz makes bigger ones that scrub tougher deposits. Read the number on the listing and pick 46 to 48 kHz for jewelry and retainers, and 40 kHz only for sturdy hardware.

Ultrasonic units hum and sometimes whine, which matters if it sits in a bedroom. Only the UMPOPO under 38dB and KUNPHY below 45dB publish a figure. If a listing is silent on decibels, assume it is louder and avoid placing it near sleeping areas.

A timer protects both the item and the transducer. Short cycles of 3 to 5 minutes suit light soil, while 10 minutes or more handles tarnish. Look for adjustable or multiple durations, and be cautious with fixed long cycles on plated pieces.

Retainer cleaners often add a UV lamp. It is a convenience step that runs after ultrasonic cleaning, not a substitute for brushing, and listings rarely provide measured output. Treat it as a bonus, and check that the UV stage can run separately like the Clelifove's UV-only mode.

faq.q: Can I clean eyeglasses in these units?
faq.a: Only the Magnasonic 20oz (600 ml) and VEVOR 1.3 L have tanks large enough for most frames. The 350 ml and 200 ml pods such as the OSLTWI and Clelifove are sized for rings, chains and retainers.

faq.q: What mistake do people make with ultrasonic cleaners?
faq.a: Choosing a 40 kHz unit like the VEVOR for delicate jewelry. Soft stones, pearls and plated pieces can be damaged. Stick to 46 to 48 kHz models such as the OSLTWI or KUNPHY for those.

faq.q: Is the UMPOPO worth it over the Clelifove?
faq.a: If noise matters, yes. The UMPOPO claims under 38dB, while the Clelifove lists no figure. The Clelifove offers a two-year warranty and a UV-only mode, so pick it if longevity matters more.

faq.q: How do I use one the first time?
faq.a: Fill to the line with water and a drop of mild detergent, set the timer, and place items in the basket if one is included, as with the Magnasonic. Start with a short cycle and repeat if needed.

faq.q: How do I maintain the tank?
faq.a: Empty it after use and wipe the stainless steel dry to prevent mineral spots. The OSLTWI and VEVOR use 304 stainless, which resists rust, but avoid abrasive pads that scratch the tank.

faq.q: Can I run it without liquid?
faq.a: No. Running any of these units empty can damage the transducer, because the water carries the energy away. Always fill past the minimum line, whether it is the KUNPHY or the Magnasonic.

finalTake: The Magnasonic 20oz is the best single purchase, because it handles glasses, jewelry and small tools with five modes. Choose the UMPOPO if the cleaner sits near a bed and holds retainers, and the Clelifove if you want the longest warranty. Treat the VEVOR as the heavy-duty pick, and avoid 40 kHz for soft stones.
